papers.title: Learning to Think and Explore in 3D World
papers.tldr: ACT3D trains a vision-language model to actively navigate 3D environments and gather only the visual evidence needed to answer questions.

papers.abstract: Multi-modal semantic segmentation benefits from complementary sensors, but this benefit is fragile when some modalities are degraded or missing at test time. Many existing methods rely on dedicated fusion modules or multi-branch cross-modal encoders, and the fusion often becomes unreliable when modalities are absent, leading to substantial performance drops. We propose \textbf{FuseAdapt}, a parameter-efficient framework that performs fusion within the adaptation space of a frozen vision foundation model (VFM), exploring whether VFM priors can serve as an effective shared backbone for multi-modal segmentation. Instead of attaching a standalone fusion network, FuseAdapt assigns each modality a lightweight adaptation branch and performs \emph{adaptation-space fusion} by keeping Q/V low-rank adaptation private to each modality and routing only FFN low-rank residual activations across modalities inside the frozen backbone. The pretrained VFM remains fixed while modality-specific corrections and explicit cross-modal interaction are learned through the adaptation paths. To handle missing modalities, we further introduce \textbf{Predictive Modality Modeling (PMM)}, a direct representation-level objective for cross-modal redundancy. During training, PMM masks a target modality and predicts its embedding from the visible ones, supervised by a teacher target computed under full-modality input. PMM is used only during training and adds no inference-time overhead. Across three multi-modal segmentation benchmarks (MCubeS, DELIVER, MUSES), FuseAdapt consistently improves both modality-complete and modality-incomplete segmentation with a small trainable budget, yielding up to +3.01 mIoU under full modalities and +12.56 mIoU under missing modalities over prior state-of-the-art. Project page: https://devinxzhang.github.io/FuseAdapt-Page/.
bullets: Addresses performance degradation when modalities are absent or corrupted at test time.
Uses modality-specific low-rank adaptation branches inside a frozen vision foundation model.
Fuses modalities by routing only FFN adaptation residuals across modalities while keeping Q/V adaptations private.
Introduces Predictive Modality Modeling to reconstruct masked modality embeddings during training without inference overhead.
Improves complete- and incomplete-modality segmentation across three benchmarks, with gains of up to 3.01 and 12.56 mIoU, respectively.
papers.selection_reason: Parameter-efficient multimodal fusion in a frozen vision foundation model; relevant to efficient adaptation and spatial segmentation.
papers.title: FuseAdapt: Parameter-Efficient Multimodal Fusion for Semantic Segmentation with Missing Modalities
papers.tldr: FuseAdapt enables robust multimodal semantic segmentation with missing sensors by learning lightweight cross-modal adaptations within a frozen vision foundation model.

papers.abstract: Distilling vision-language features into 3D Gaussian Splatting yields a language map that can be queried with arbitrary text. In deployment, however, a small set of user-specified targets must be reliably located, which current distilled maps often miss, while open-vocabulary queryability for other words must remain intact. We propose a training-free, target-aware refinement of an already-distilled language map. Guided by a text-promptable segmenter, the visual embedding inside each detected target region is blended with the target text embedding, a convex combination whose coefficient sets the amount of injected prior, while non-target regions are left untouched. Injecting too much overwrites appearance cues and general queryability, so we seek, for each target, the smallest coefficient that still lets it win, and we obtain every coefficient in closed form, leaving no hyperparameters to tune. We further identify a failure mode of injection in language-goal localization. Text embeddings share a common component, and injecting them makes the standard cosine read-out query-agnostic, which a centering step in the read-out removes. Across three benchmarks, the refinement consistently improves open-vocabulary segmentation, roughly doubling the base mIoU on Replica, and localizes language goals more reliably than the base map. It also transfers as a plug-in to off-the-shelf field-based and object-level language maps and supports a real-world demonstration in which a legged robot navigates to natural-language goals. Project page and code: https://lab-of-ai-and-robotics.github.io/target-aware-langmap/
authors: Sibaek Lee, Kyeongsu Kang, Seongbo Ha, Yewon Jeon, Joonyeol Choi, Daegeol Ko, Jaehyuk Hur, Taemin Choi, Minsu Kim, Hyungjoo Ahn, Wonsok Yoo, Hyeonwoo Yu
bullets: Addresses missed user-specified targets in distilled 3D language maps without sacrificing other-word queryability.
Uses a text-promptable segmenter to blend target-region visual embeddings with target text embeddings, leaving non-target regions unchanged.
Computes the smallest effective blending coefficient in closed form, avoiding tuning hyperparameters.
Centers the read-out to remove query-agnostic effects caused by shared components in text embeddings.
Improves open-vocabulary segmentation across three benchmarks, roughly doubling base mIoU on Replica, and transfers to other language maps and real-world robot navigation.
papers.selection_reason: Training-free refinement of 3D language maps for target localization.
papers.title: Training-Free Target-Aware Refinement of 3D Gaussian Language Map
papers.tldr: A training-free refinement makes 3D Gaussian language maps reliably detect specified targets while preserving open-vocabulary querying and improving language-goal navigation.

papers.abstract: Audio-visual large language models (AV-LLMs) have made strong progress in multimodal understanding, yet most treat audio as monaural semantic content, limiting their ability to reason about where sounds originate and how they relate to the visual scene. Recent spatial audio-visual studies address parts of this problem, but often focus on specific abilities, such as spatial correspondence or direction and distance reasoning. In this work, we introduce HLR-AVSceneQA, a comprehensive benchmark with a hear-localize-reason hierarchy that evaluates whether models can recognize what is heard, localize sound sources in egocentric and allocentric views, and use these localized sources to reason about how they relate to the visual scene. We further introduce HLR-LLM, which augments a strong audio-visual foundation model with a binaural spatial audio branch alongside its monaural semantic audio pathway. We train HLR-LLM with a curriculum that incorporates final-stage chain-of-thought supervision for multi-step spatial reasoning. Experiments show that existing AV-LLMs remain limited in spatial grounding and relational reasoning, while HLR-LLM substantially improves spatial audio-visual scene understanding without compromising semantic audio-visual perception.
authors: Kim Sung-Bin, Lee Jung-Mok, Jinwoo Jung, Oh Hyun-Bin, Hyeonggon Ryu, David Harwath, Tae-Hyun Oh

Introduces HLR-AVSceneQA, a hierarchical benchmark covering recognition, egocentric/allocentric localization, and scene-relative reasoning.
Presents HLR-LLM with binaural spatial audio and monaural semantic audio pathways.
Uses curriculum training with final-stage chain-of-thought supervision for multi-step spatial reasoning.
Experiments show improved spatial audio-visual understanding without compromising semantic perception; existing AV-LLMs remain limited in spatial grounding and relational reasoning.
papers.selection_reason: Spatially aware audio-visual LLM with binaural spatial branch and spatial reasoning benchmark, fitting multimodal LLM and spatial intelligence.
papers.title: Hear, Localize, and Reason: Spatially Aware Scene Understanding for Audio-Visual LLMs
papers.tldr: HLR-AVSceneQA and HLR-LLM enable audio-visual models to hear, localize, and reason about sounds in relation to visual scenes.

papers.abstract: Residential design aims to transform existing homes into functional living spaces while satisfying diverse design preferences and physical constraints. However, existing floorplan generation methods typically assume empty building boundaries as input, whereas renovation requires reasoning over existing floorplans. Furthermore, floorplan renovation and furniture layout are commonly addressed as separate tasks, overlooking their inherent spatial dependency. Consequently, practical residential design must preserve immutable structural components while transforming editable spatial elements. It must also optimize furniture placement under design objectives and physical constraints. To address these challenges, we formulate residential design as a design-point-guided conditional generation task and propose RenoLayout, a framework that translates a pre-design residential state together with a design-point set into an executable Geometry-as-Code program. To enable controllable supervision, we construct a Design Map comprising 123 fine-grained design points covering structural renovation and furniture layout. We further introduce Difference-Grounded Design-Point Annotation to derive design-point sets automatically from before--after design pairs with VLM-based consistency verification. RenoLayout is trained using a three-stage CPT--SFT--RL pipeline, progressively improving spatial reasoning, instruction following, and constraint compliance. We also introduce the RenoLayout Benchmark, a set of 200 real-world before--after renovation cases with complete furniture layouts. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first benchmark for unified residential design. These cases include design-critical structural and building-service constraints.
authors: Jingguo Liu, Yuanqing Liu, Chong Zhang, Yue Yang
bullets: Addresses the gap between methods that generate empty-boundary floorplans and practical renovation of existing homes.
Models renovation and furniture layout jointly while preserving immutable structural components and satisfying physical constraints.
Introduces a 123-point Design Map and VLM-verified annotation method to derive design guidance from before–after examples.
Trains the framework with a three-stage CPT–SFT–RL pipeline for spatial reasoning, instruction following, and constraint compliance.
Provides the RenoLayout Benchmark with 200 real-world renovation cases containing complete furniture layouts and design-critical constraints.
papers.selection_reason: Unified floorplan renovation and furniture layout with spatial reasoning and constraint compliance; directly relevant to spatial intelligence.
papers.title: RenoLayout: Unified Floorplan Renovation and Furniture Layout for Constraint-Aware Residential Design
papers.tldr: RenoLayout unifies residential floorplan renovation and furniture placement by generating executable Geometry-as-Code designs from existing layouts, design points, and structural constraints.

papers.abstract: Detailed captions transfer visual information into vision-language model supervision, but quality is easily conflated with length: long single-pass outputs still miss small objects, text, and spatial relations or promote uncertain observations into confident claims. We formulate fine-grained captioning as recoverable visual information transfer, in which a teacher acquires missing evidence under a finite observation budget and converts it into reusable supervision. ZoomCap uses a draft caption to route conditional knowledge retrieval, OCR-sensitive reading, coverage-gap recovery, and adaptive visual zooming, allocating deeper crops only to the most complex eligible region, deriving spatial relations from grounded geometry, and fusing non-duplicate evidence. We also introduce FactCycle, which scores caption-derived atomic claims on two blind anchors--source image (truthfulness) and reconstruction (realizability)--separating fabrication from generator loss claim by claim; human and multi-judge comparisons complement this fact-level view. Against Qwen3.5-397B-A17B captions, ZoomCap achieves an 81.9% human tie-adjusted preference score with a teacher over 10x smaller, and FactCycle counts 52.4 transferred claims per image vs. 31.5 for ScaleCap. The evidence also transfers: in continual pre-training, ZoomCap-450K improves the 11-benchmark average by 1.31-2.38 points over the strongest competing corpus and Ling-Tiny-VL-v3 gains 1.4 points on a production document/OCR monitor suite (1.5 on perception) at 60B tokens; in medical pre-training, 2.64M ZoomCap-captioned images improve five VQA benchmarks by 3.04 points (vs. 1.76 for same-image Gemini-3.1-Pro captions).
authors: Hao Shi, Jiafeng Wang, Yuzhuo Fu, Tao Zhang, Jian Bai, Juelu Zhang, Qing Cui, Chao Huang
bullets: Targets missed small objects, text, spatial relations, and overconfident unsupported claims in long single-pass captions.
Routes a draft caption to conditional retrieval, OCR-sensitive reading, coverage recovery, adaptive region zooming, and grounded spatial reasoning under a fixed observation budget.
Introduces FactCycle, which evaluates atomic claims against both the source image and reconstructed scene to distinguish fabrication from information loss.
Achieves an 81.9% human tie-adjusted preference score and transfers 52.4 claims per image versus 31.5 for ScaleCap.
ZoomCap-based pre-training improves general, document/OCR, and medical VQA performance across the reported benchmarks.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a method for transferring visual information to VLMs via evidence-routed zooming. This improves the spatial reasoning capabilities of multimodal models by grounding them in specific visual details.
papers.title: ZoomCap: Evidence-Routed Visual Zooming for Recoverable Visual Information Transfer
papers.tldr: ZoomCap uses evidence-guided visual zooming and claim-level verification to produce more detailed, reliable captions that transfer effectively to vision-language model training.

papers.abstract: Panoramic 3D reconstruction enables the holistic recovery of complete 360 $^\circ$ scene geometry, offering significant benefits for robotics and AR/VR applications. However, directly estimating geometry from ERP images is inherently challenged by spherical distortions. To reduce spherical projection distortions, a common strategy is to decompose panoramas into distortion-free perspective views, but independently processing these views often introduces cross-view geometric inconsistencies. To address these challenges, we introduce GeoPano, a feed-forward framework for single-view panoramic 3D reconstruction that recovers a geometrically accurate and consistent point cloud from a single panorama. Our approach is driven by two key innovations: First, we propose a panoramic-aware attention aggregator, featuring a streamlined attention architecture equipped with a novel Pano-Attention mechanism, which explicitly exploits the intrinsic spherical geometry of the panorama to guide cross-view interactions, thereby suppressing geometric inconsistencies. Furthermore, we formulate a hybrid supervision strategy to jointly enforce fine-grained local details in perspective space and global structural coherence in spherical space. Experiments demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms previous SOTA approaches in reconstruction accuracy, geometric consistency, and visual fidelity.
authors: Jing OU, Zidong Cao, Liaoyuan Fan, Zhuoxiao Li, Shuai Zhang, Yinrui Ren, Dongli Wu, Haoang Li, Hui Xiong, Wufan Zhao
bullets: Addresses ERP spherical distortions and inconsistencies caused by independently processing perspective views.
Uses a panoramic-aware attention aggregator with a Pano-Attention mechanism for geometry-guided cross-view interaction.
Combines perspective-space supervision for local detail with spherical-space supervision for global structural coherence.
Experiments report improved reconstruction accuracy, geometric consistency, and visual fidelity over prior state-of-the-art methods.
papers.selection_reason: Develops a framework for 3D reconstruction from panoramas that explicitly handles spherical geometry. This contributes to spatial intelligence by improving geometric reasoning and 3D-aware understanding in multimodal models.
papers.title: GeoPano: Towards Geometrically Accurate 3D Reconstruction from a Single Panorama
papers.tldr: GeoPano reconstructs geometrically consistent 3D point clouds from a single panorama by modeling spherical geometry and combining local and global supervision.

papers.abstract: Post-hoc image explanations usually show where a model looks using spatial heatmaps or indicate which channels matter using global channel scores. These separate views are limiting for multispectral data because channel relevance is often spatially localized and physically meaningful. We introduce Spectral-Spatial Interpretation (SSI), a full-grid attribution method over position-channel players (g,c). For each spatial position, SSI fixes the observed surrounding context, defines a conditional game over the channels at that position, and applies the Shapley value to this local game. The result is a full spectral-spatial attribution matrix rather than a single heatmap or a global channel ranking. SSI has a clear local interpretation. It satisfies Shapley fairness within each position, and aggregating its channel attributions exactly recovers the position-level contextual contrast obtained by replacing that position with the baseline. SSI also differs from context-averaged Owen-style hierarchical accounting, which uses the same position-channel grouping but averages over external spatial coalitions. On HLS Burn Scar, SSI outperforms an MC-Owen estimator across retained attribution metrics while using only about 6% of its evaluation budget. Across CUB-200, EuroSAT, and HLS Burn Scar under both per-channel mean and zero baselines, SSI achieves the best joint deletion and insertion AUC over dense, flat, and rank-1 baselines, yields the strongest spectral hit rates and channel deletion, and leads spatial localization on both annotated datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/AtheavenMa/Spectral-Spatial-Interpretation.
authors: Haotian Ma, Ruqi Yang, Philip Townsend
bullets: Addresses the limitation of separate spatial heatmaps and global channel scores when channel relevance varies across locations.
Defines a conditional local game over channels at each position while holding surrounding context fixed.
Provides Shapley fairness locally and exactly recovers each position’s contextual contrast when channel attributions are aggregated.
Across three datasets and two baselines, SSI achieves the strongest reported deletion/insertion, spectral, channel, and spatial-localization metrics.
On HLS Burn Scar, it outperforms an MC-Owen estimator using about 6% of its evaluation budget.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces Spectral-Spatial Interpretation for multispectral data, a method for attribution that explicitly models spatial and channel relationships, relevant to spatial intelligence.
papers.title: Spectral-Spatial Interpretation
papers.tldr: SSI explains multispectral model predictions by assigning Shapley-based importance to each spatial position–channel pair, producing a detailed spectral-spatial attribution map.

papers.abstract: Spatial agents have access to reconstruction and segmentation tools, yet inconsistent predictions and fragmented object identities can prevent their outputs from becoming reliable 3D scene information. A simple oracle experiment exposes this perception bottleneck: replacing tool-predicted perception with ground-truth 3D bounding boxes raises an agent to nearly full score across five object-centric VSI-Bench tasks, while retaining the same reasoning tools. Motivated by this finding, we believe the devil of spatial reasoning lies in 3D itself, and introduce DeSpatial(Devil of Spatial), which explicitly decomposes spatial understanding into perception and reasoning. DeSpatial has a shared 3D perception tool to reconcile independent perception outputs into a unified, metric, gravity-aligned 3D scene. This perception tool has two core components: a) a joint segmentation--depth co-refinement module that consolidates masks of the same object and removes projection artifacts caused by inconsistent segmentation and depth within a single frame; b) a cross-view instance fusion module that consolidate voxel-overlapping instances but not allowed to merge same-frame instances. This fusion module additionally fuses spatially disjoint fragments caused by insufficient multi-view observations, by checking their 3D structure and source mask appearance. After receiving the complete and unified 3D scene information, the agent chooses reasoning or computational tools to solve the spatial problem. DeSpatial achieves leading performance on VSI-Bench, MindCube-Tiny, and ViewSpatial, with additional long-video results on VSI-SUPER, revealing the bottleneck of spatial understanding lies in a precise 3D perception itself.
authors: Yifei Liu, Xiaolong Zhou, Ziyang Gong, Yifan Zhou, Yuanyuan Gao, Yuning Gong, Yuchen Yang, Hongjie Zhang, Xue Yang, Xiao Sun, Zhihang Zhong
bullets: An oracle experiment finds that ground-truth 3D boxes nearly solve five object-centric VSI-Bench tasks, exposing perception as the main bottleneck.
DeSpatial explicitly separates 3D perception from downstream reasoning and computation.
Its shared perception tool builds a metric, gravity-aligned scene using joint segmentation–depth refinement and cross-view instance fusion.
The system prevents erroneous merges while reconnecting fragmented instances using 3D structure and mask appearance.
It achieves leading performance on VSI-Bench, MindCube-Tiny, and ViewSpatial, with additional long-video evaluation on VSI-SUPER.
papers.selection_reason: Agentic spatial reasoning decomposed into unified 3D perception and reasoning; directly relevant to spatial intelligence and 3D scene understanding.
papers.title: DeSpatial: The devil of Agentic Spatial Reasoning Lies in 3D Itself
papers.tldr: DeSpatial shows that reliable agentic spatial reasoning depends primarily on accurate, unified 3D perception rather than reasoning alone.

papers.abstract: Map generation tasks feature extensive non-structural vectorized data (e.g., points, polylines, and polygons) and thus pose significant challenges to common pixel-wise generative models. Conventional approaches use multiple stages, first segmenting these features at the pixel level and then performing vectorized post-processing, with errors and complexity compounding at each stage. Motivated by the recent success of auto-regressive language modeling, we propose the first map foundation model, named Map Auto-Regressor (MARS), that is capable of generating both multi-polyline road networks and polygon buildings in a unified manner. For training MARS, we collected to our knowledge the largest multi-class map extraction dataset totaling 3.4M examples, which we call MAP-3M. Across four road and building datasets, MARS outperforms or matches the performance of multistage baselines. Additionally, we develop a "Chat with MARS" capability that enables interactive human-in-the-loop map generation and correction, supported by the auto-regressive nature of our end-to-end approach. We release our MAP-3M dataset and project demo page at (1) https://huggingface.co/datasets/bag-lab/MAP-3M and (2) https://huggingface.co/spaces/bag-lab/MARS, respectively.
authors: Qi Zhang, Suvam Bag, Rupanjali Kukal, Lucas Thai, Jacob Kovarskiy, Mike Bianco, Xiaojie Guo, Raphael Tang, Mikael Figueroa, Rishi Madhok, Nikolaos Karianakis, Fuxun Yu
bullets: Addresses the complexity and error accumulation of conventional pixel-wise, multistage map-generation pipelines.
Unifies generation of multi-polyline roads and polygon buildings in an end-to-end autoregressive framework.
Trained on MAP-3M, a 3.4M-example multi-class map extraction dataset.
Across four road and building datasets, matches or surpasses multistage baselines.
Supports interactive human correction through a “Chat with MARS” capability; the dataset and demo are released publicly.
papers.selection_reason: Autoregressive map foundation model generating vectorized road networks and buildings; directly relevant to spatial layout understanding and spatial intelligence.
papers.title: MARS - A foundational map auto-regressor
papers.tldr: MARS is an autoregressive foundation model that directly generates vectorized road networks and building polygons, avoiding multistage pixel segmentation and post-processing.

papers.abstract: Generating novel views from limited observations requires preserving both the appearance and spatial structure of a scene. Although recent approaches exploit fine-grained geometric cues, they do not explicitly model high-level semantic and spatial properties such as object identity, attributes, and inter-object relationships. In this work, we investigate whether 3D language understanding can provide complementary supervision for novel-view generation. We introduce Ask4NV, built on a pretrained unified multimodal model with a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture. Our model incorporates camera geometry into both VAE and ViT representations and leverages understanding features during generation through joint self-attention with a modality-aware attention masking strategy. Experiments demonstrate strong image quality and geometric consistency in novel-view generation, alongside competitive 3D language understanding. Further analysis shows that joint training improves cross-view correspondence in VAE representations and similarity in a 3D-aware feature space.
authors: Jahyeok Koo, Hyeonseo Yu, Seungho Jang, Jaewoo Jung, Jiwon Kang, Seokju Cho, Seungryong Kim
bullets: Targets the challenge of preserving both scene appearance and spatial structure from limited observations.
Introduces Ask4NV, built on a pretrained unified multimodal Mixture-of-Transformers model.
Encodes camera geometry in VAE and ViT representations and integrates understanding features via masked joint self-attention.
Achieves strong image quality and geometric consistency while maintaining competitive 3D language understanding.
Joint training improves cross-view correspondence and 3D-aware feature similarity.
papers.selection_reason: Investigates using 3D language understanding (spatial questions) to supervise novel-view generation. This combines 3D reasoning with generative models, relevant to 3D foundation models and spatial intelligence.
papers.title: Can Learning to Answer Spatial Questions Improve Novel-View Generation?
papers.tldr: Ask4NV uses 3D language understanding and camera-aware multimodal modeling to improve the visual quality and geometric consistency of novel-view generation.

papers.abstract: Achieving general spatial intelligence requires a unified understanding of both static 3D and dynamic 4D. However, we find that existing models struggle to excel at both: 3D post-training can weaken dynamic understanding, while 4D-specialized models often lack strong static 3D reasoning. Our analysis reveals that this spatial--dynamic interference is highly non-uniform across parameter groups, with the balance between static and dynamic capabilities particularly sensitive to changes in late-layer MLPs. To address this interference, we propose DynThinker, a unified framework for jointly strengthening static and dynamic spatial reasoning. Decoupled Exponential Moving Average (D-EMA) applies configurable group-wise averaging to constrain drift in interference-sensitive pretrained parameters while preserving flexibility for capability enhancement. Spatial-Dynamic Fusion (SDF) complements D-EMA by selectively integrating spatial and temporal priors from a dynamic geometry encoder into intermediate VLM representations under semantic guidance. Across ten metrics spanning nine static 3D and dynamic 4D benchmarks, DynThinker achieves the highest average score among all evaluated models. Notably, DynThinker achieves 56.0 on ReVSI, 67.2 on DSR-Bench, and 51.2 and 40.1 under the sample-wise and group-wise evaluation protocols of DSI-Bench, respectively, setting new state-of-the-art results among the compared open-source models across all four evaluations within a unified model.
authors: Qihang Cao, Haoyuan Li, Zihan Guo, Sensen Gao, Zihui Gao, Huixin Zhang, Fan He, Jianhua Han, Hang Xu, Xiaodan Liang, Jia-Wang Bian
bullets: Existing models face a trade-off: improving static 3D reasoning can harm dynamic understanding, while 4D-specialized models may underperform on static tasks.
The interference is non-uniform across parameters and is especially sensitive to late-layer MLP changes.
Decoupled Exponential Moving Average (D-EMA) stabilizes interference-sensitive parameter groups while allowing capability improvements elsewhere.
Spatial-Dynamic Fusion (SDF) selectively injects temporal and spatial priors from a dynamic geometry encoder into intermediate vision-language representations.
Across ten metrics on nine benchmarks, DynThinker obtains the highest average score among evaluated models and sets open-source results on four reported evaluations.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a unified framework (DynThinker) for static 3D and dynamic 4D spatial reasoning in VLMs, addressing the interference between these capabilities through decoupled EMA and spatial-dynamic fusion. This directly addresses spatial reasoning and geometry-aware multimodal models.
papers.title: DynThinker: Unifying Static 3D and Dynamic 4D Spatial Reasoning
papers.tldr: DynThinker unifies static 3D and dynamic 4D spatial reasoning by mitigating interference between the two capabilities.

papers.abstract: Existing geometry-aware Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) increasingly rely on external 3D encoders to provide structural priors, but executing these additional encoder paths at inference introduces substantial latency and computational overhead. We propose GeoThinker-$F$, an efficient framework that internalizes spatiotemporal perception by transforming causal MLLM hidden states into predictive latent world representations. Our key insight is that intermediate semantic representations contain sufficient information to predict useful representations of current geometry and future semantics, without requiring an exact reproduction of features from a dedicated 3D encoder. To realize this idea, GeoThinker-$F$ adopts a decoupled two-stage training strategy. In the first stage, the MLLM backbone is frozen while lightweight Latent Frame Prediction (LFP) heads learn from an offline 3D geometry expert and next-frame semantic targets. In the second stage, the external expert is removed, and the model is jointly optimized to generate and selectively integrate its self-predicted priors through a specialized Spatial-Grounded Temporal (SGT) Fusion module. Extensive evaluations show that GeoThinker-$F$ eliminates runtime dependence on external 3D geometry encoders while maintaining competitive performance across diverse spatial intelligence benchmarks. It achieves up to a $3.6\times$ inference speedup, reducing latency from $1.45\,\mathrm{s}$ to $0.40\,\mathrm{s}$ while retaining strong spatial reasoning performance.
authors: Haoyuan Li, Qihang Cao, Huanyuan Zhou, Xin Hu, Sijia Chen, Zihan Guo, Kun Xiang, Yunshuang Nie, Tao Tang, Xinlong Zheng, Jia-Wang Bian, Xianming Liu, Xiaodan Liang
bullets: Addresses the latency and computational overhead caused by external 3D geometry encoders in geometry-aware MLLMs.
Transforms intermediate MLLM hidden states into predictive representations of current geometry and future semantics.
Uses two-stage training: lightweight latent frame prediction heads first learn from geometry and next-frame semantic targets, then the external expert is removed during joint optimization.
Introduces Spatial-Grounded Temporal Fusion to selectively integrate self-predicted spatial-temporal priors.
Reports latency reduction from 1.45 s to 0.40 s while retaining competitive performance across diverse spatial intelligence benchmarks.
papers.selection_reason: Geometry-aware MLLM with predictive world representations and faster spatial intelligence inference.
papers.title: GeoThinker-$F$: Endogenous Predictive World Representations for Fast Spatial Intelligence
papers.tldr: GeoThinker-F internalizes spatial and temporal world representations in an MLLM, removing external 3D encoders and achieving up to 3.6× faster inference while maintaining strong spatial reasoning.

papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models have made significant progress in referring expression comprehension (REC), yet most REC benchmarks still focus on final-target localization. Complex queries often involve intermediate visual references with different dependencies on prior grounding, but final-only evaluation leaves this process unexamined. To address this gap, we formulate trajectory-level REC, in which models receive an ordered sequence of grounding steps constructed from a single complex query and localize the target regions associated with each step. We instantiate this setting in ReferFlow-Bench, which characterizes structured region transitions through four trajectory types, namely Refinement, Shift, Reset, and Mixture. Experiments show that current models struggle to consistently ground intermediate visual references across successive steps. We further propose ReferFlow, which decouples interleaved text-latent trajectory generation from coordinate decoding. Specifically, Stateful Region Latent Reasoning represents each target region as an object-indexed state composed of continuous latents, with explicit visual and spatial supervision to preserve region information for subsequent grounding. Trajectory-Aware Parallel Decoding then recovers all coordinate blocks in parallel through four geometry-constrained refinement rounds, with each block conditioned on its corresponding trajectory prefix, thereby reducing within-box sequential dependencies and eliminating cross-box autoregression. We further apply Grounding-Aware GRPO to promote consistent grounding across steps and learn adaptive trajectory generation from complex REC queries. ReferFlow achieves leading performance on general REC benchmarks and ReferFlow-Bench.
authors: Tianyi Gao, Han Fang, Xin Wei, Yaoyao Zhong, Zhaoyan Pan, Weijie Zhu, Hongbo Sun, Zhiyu Lin, Kaicheng Yang, Jinglin Xu, Ye Yuan, Hao Li, Hao Sun, Jingmin Xin
bullets: Introduces trajectory-level REC, evaluating ordered grounding steps rather than only the final target.
Presents ReferFlow-Bench with four region-transition types: Refinement, Shift, Reset, and Mixture.
Uses stateful region latent reasoning to preserve visual and spatial information across grounding steps.
Employs trajectory-aware parallel coordinate decoding with geometry-constrained refinement to reduce sequential dependencies.
Grounding-Aware GRPO encourages consistent multi-step grounding; ReferFlow achieves leading performance on general REC benchmarks and ReferFlow-Bench.
papers.selection_reason: Addresses complex referring expressions in MLLMs using trajectory-level grounding and geometry-constrained refinement, advancing spatial reasoning capabilities.
papers.title: ReferFlow: Beyond Final-Target Localization for Complex Referring Expressions
papers.tldr: ReferFlow extends referring expression comprehension from final-target localization to step-by-step grounding of intermediate visual references, improving trajectory-level reasoning.

papers.abstract: Document understanding systems are typically evaluated as separate components via layout analysis, optical text recognition, reading-order prediction, and image captioning. This separation leaves scientific figures, captions, and visual semantics weakly connected, and fails to measure whether a model can produce a single page-level parse that is both structurally faithful and semantically accessible. We introduce Read-Parse-Describe, a unified dataset for document parsing with visual element description generation. Given a page image, models are required to output an ordered list of layout elements containing bounding boxes, semantic labels, reading-order indices, recognized textual content, and alternative text descriptions for visual elements. The benchmark is built from 2,402 documents, comprising 18,163 continuous pages, 125,218 layout elements, and 11,338 visual instances. Besides, we further propose a plug-and-play space-awareness enhancer that reuses multi-layer visual features and injects grid-aware spatial guidance into vision-language tokens for layout-aware generation. Experiments across end-to-end VLMs and pipeline parsers show that existing systems still struggle to jointly recover reading order and visual semantics, while our enhanced model achieves strong joint performance. These results highlight the need to move beyond isolated document parsing modules toward unified models that jointly read, parse, and describe complex documents. The new dataset and code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/yufanchen96/RPD
authors: Yuheng Chen, Yufan Chen, Zhuojun Cai, Ruiping Liu, Junwei Zheng, Jiale Wei, Di Wen, Weijia Fan, Kunyu Peng, Jiaming Zhang, Rainer Stiefelhagen
bullets: Targets the limitations of evaluating layout analysis, OCR, reading order, and image captioning as separate tasks.
Requires page-level outputs combining ordered layout elements, bounding boxes, semantic labels, recognized text, and visual-element descriptions.
The dataset contains 2,402 documents, 18,163 pages, 125,218 layout elements, and 11,338 visual instances.
Adds a plug-and-play space-awareness enhancer that injects grid-guided spatial information into vision-language tokens.
Experiments show existing systems struggle to jointly recover reading order and visual semantics, while the enhanced model achieves strong joint performance.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a unified document parsing dataset and a space-awareness enhancer for VLMs, explicitly incorporating grid-aware spatial guidance into vision-language tokens.
papers.title: Read, Parse, Describe: Unified Document Parsing with Visual Element Description Generation
papers.tldr: Read-Parse-Describe introduces a benchmark and spatially enhanced model for jointly parsing document structure, text, reading order, and visual semantics from page images.

papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of large vision language models (LVLMs) has made geolocation inference from images highly accurate and accessible. This poses serious privacy risks: a passive adversary with black-box LVLM access can infer a user's location from a single photo with no metadata. Existing protection methods rely almost exclusively on adversarial perturbation, which introduces perceptible visual artifacts and utility degradation. We identify the visual-geolocation asymmetry: geolocation-decisive clues, such as street signs, tend to be visually peripheral but dominate location inference. Exploiting this asymmetry, we propose GeoCloak, an agentic framework for semantics-preserving geolocation privacy protection. It acts as a clue-aware planner that analyzes each image to identify geolocation-relevant clues, dispatches targeted semantic edits to directly suppress peripheral clues, and autonomously configures adversarial perturbation to further suppress residual geolocation features, all under iterative utility-aware feedback. We evaluate GeoCloak on four diverse datasets spanning 108 countries and 576 cities against five LVLMs and three inference methods. GeoCloak reduces overall city-level accuracy from 41.2% to 9.9%, approximately half of the best-performing baseline, while achieving substantially superior utility preservation both qualitatively and quantitatively. We hope this work takes a meaningful step toward practical, semantics-preserving geolocation privacy protection, giving users greater control over the location information inadvertently embedded in their shared images.
authors: Yixin Wu, Mingjie Li, Yun Shen, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang
bullets: Targets the risk that black-box vision-language models can infer locations from ordinary photos without metadata.
Exploits the asymmetry that geolocation-critical clues, such as street signs, are often visually peripheral.
Uses an agentic planner for clue detection, targeted semantic edits, adaptive perturbation, and utility-aware iteration.
Evaluated across four datasets covering 108 countries and 576 cities, with five LVLMs and three inference methods.
Reduced city-level geolocation accuracy from 41.2% to 9.9% while preserving utility better than the evaluated baselines.
papers.selection_reason: Agentic manipulation of geolocation clues in LVLMs, relevant to spatial/geolocation understanding and multimodal model robustness.
papers.title: GeoCloak: An Agentic Framework for Semantics-Preserving Geolocation Privacy via Peripheral Clue Manipulation
papers.tldr: GeoCloak protects image geolocation privacy by identifying and editing peripheral location clues while preserving overall image semantics.

papers.abstract: Interpreting an ambiguous utterance in real-world interactions often requires context beyond a single utterance. When the utterance refers to objects in a visual scene, it is necessary to maintain and update the set of plausible referents as context accumulates, without assuming that the available information identifies a unique object. However, prior work on interactive visual grounding, which localizes objects referred to by linguistic expressions, has focused on identifying a unique object once sufficient dialogue context becomes available. To address this gap, we propose Candidate Set Visual Grounding (CSVG), a task for estimating the set of objects consistent with the given dialogue context. We further introduce CandVG, a benchmark that evaluates how the candidate set changes across dialogue turns. Our evaluation of vision-language models shows that stronger visual grounding capability does not necessarily yield better CSVG performance. In particular, models have difficulty predicting the complete candidate set, owing to challenges in candidate generation and premature commitment to a small set of candidates in early turns. Nevertheless, we find that this limitation can be partially mitigated in the evaluated large-scale models using instructions designed for CSVG.
authors: Shun Inadumi, Lee Sangmyeong, Koichiro Yoshino
bullets: Ambiguous referring expressions may remain compatible with multiple scene objects as dialogue unfolds.
Candidate Set Visual Grounding (CSVG) estimates the full set of plausible referents rather than selecting one object.
CandVG benchmarks how candidate sets change across dialogue turns.
Stronger conventional visual grounding does not necessarily improve CSVG performance.
CSVG-specific instructions partially mitigate incomplete candidate generation in evaluated large-scale models.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a visual grounding task for ambiguous dialogue, evaluating vision-language models and spatial referent understanding.
papers.title: Recognizing Dialogue Ambiguity via Candidate Set Visual Grounding
papers.tldr: CSVG reframes visual grounding as tracking all objects consistent with ambiguous dialogue, revealing that current vision-language models often miss candidates and commit too early.

papers.abstract: Real-world engineering drawings are often large-format and information-dense. Answering practical engineering questions therefore requires both fine-grained understanding of engineering information and complex reasoning over objects, relations, and evidence distributed across different regions or views. Existing benchmarks cover a range of engineering-drawing understanding tasks involving local regions, individual views, specific elements, or more constrained visual settings. However, systematic evaluation of understanding over realistic, large-format engineering drawings remains limited. To address this gap, we introduce LED-BENCH, a multidisciplinary benchmark designed to evaluate fine-grained understanding and complex reasoning over large-format engineering drawings, spanning the mechanical, architectural, and transportation domains. Extensive evaluation of 11 representative multimodal large language models, including 8 proprietary models and 3 open-source models, reveals substantial remaining difficulty: GPT-5.6 Sol achieves 52.65% average accuracy, performance varies across engineering domains, and all evaluated models perform worse on questions requiring broader evidence integration. These results highlight fine-grained understanding, evidence integration, and complex reasoning over large-format engineering drawings as persistent challenges for current multimodal models.
authors: Ke Li, Tianyi Wang, Enning You, Chaoqun Wan, Zhen Huang, Shuxian Liang, Xian-Sheng Hua
bullets: Covers mechanical, architectural, and transportation engineering domains.
Tests reasoning over objects, relations, and evidence distributed across regions and views.
Evaluates 11 multimodal large language models, including proprietary and open-source systems.
Models struggle particularly with questions requiring broad evidence integration; GPT-5.6 Sol reaches 52.65% average accuracy.
Results identify fine-grained understanding, evidence integration, and complex reasoning as persistent challenges.
papers.selection_reason: Benchmark for MLLM understanding of large-format engineering drawings; fits multimodal LLM evaluation and spatial reasoning.
papers.title: LED-BENCH: A Benchmark for Large-format Engineering Drawing Understanding
papers.tldr: LED-BENCH evaluates multimodal models on fine-grained understanding and complex reasoning over realistic, large-format engineering drawings.

papers.abstract: A spatial answer depends on the reference frame specified in language and its supporting visual evidence. Item accuracy alone obscures whether correctness persists when either changes. We introduce Frame Evidence, a benchmark of 320 matched triplets and 960 Chinese multiple-choice questions from captured and rendered scenes. One family compares three grounded reference frames over fixed images. The other pairs image deletion annotated as insufficient with answer-preserving addition. Joint metrics require correct answers across all three frames and paired evidence variants. Across 20 configurations on 288 held-out questions, GPT three-shot reaches 50.00\% item accuracy, but the best three-frame group accuracy is 5/48 (10.42\%), reached by GPT two-shot. Few-shot prompting and task-specific adaptation improve item accuracy without consistently improving joint correctness. Input controls show where images support matched success, while repeated executions reveal answer instability beneath similar scores.
authors: Chunxi Luo, Qishuai Ding, Xingchen Peng, Hengwei Ye, Ke Zhang, Wenxin Lian, Tianyi Lu, Chunlong Yu, Zhenya Lin
bullets: Introduces 320 matched triplets and 960 Chinese multiple-choice questions from captured and rendered scenes.
Tests three grounded reference frames with fixed images, plus image deletion and answer-preserving addition variants.
Uses joint metrics requiring correct answers across all reference-frame and evidence variants.
Across 20 configurations, GPT’s best three-frame group accuracy was 5/48 (10.42%), despite 50.00% item accuracy in one setting.
Few-shot prompting and task adaptation improved individual answers but did not consistently improve joint correctness; repeated runs exposed instability.
papers.selection_reason: Benchmark for reference frames and visual evidence in multi-image spatial reasoning; fits spatial intelligence.
papers.title: Frame Evidence:A Benchmark for Reference Frames and Visual Evidence in Multi-Image Spatial Reasoning
papers.tldr: Frame Evidence shows that high item accuracy can hide poor consistency across reference frames and supporting visual evidence in multi-image spatial reasoning.

papers.abstract: Spatial intelligence requires scalable 3D environments that are both photorealistic and semantically grounded, yet existing indoor datasets are dominated by room-scale captures and costly LiDAR acquisition. Online real-estate platforms offer abundant panoramas of diverse multi-room homes, but sparse viewpoints and texture-poor regions make reconstruction severely under-constrained. We introduce Holi-Spatial 360, a generative reconstruction and data curation framework for converting these panoramas into annotated multi-room 3D environments. Because reconstruction quality bounds subsequent generation, our Correspondence-Guided Geometric Optimization converts feed-forward reconstruction priors into reliable cross-view constraints and builds a coherent 3D Gaussian Splatting representation as 3D spatial memory. Adapted single-image and video priors then restore appearance and complete continuous trajectories while preserving observed content. The reconstructed scenes support arbitrary RGB-D rendering and an automated curation pipeline that combines end-to-end 3D grounding with VLM-based verification. Holi360 contains over 1K multi-room 3DGS scenes, more than 100K instance annotations, and 2M spatial question-answer pairs. We also introduce the Holi360 benchmark to evaluate the spatial understanding of VLMs in real-world, multi-room indoor environments. Experiments demonstrate superior reconstruction and curation quality under sparse panoramic inputs, while fine-tuning VLMs on Holi360 substantially improves spatial reasoning capabilities.
authors: Yuanyuan Gao, Zhirui Liu, Yuning Gong, Yifei Liu, Yifan Zhan, Kuixuan Jiao, Xiaolong Zhou, Yifan Yang, Hongjie Zhang, Xue Yang, Dan Xu, Zhihang Zhong
bullets: Addresses the scarcity of scalable, photorealistic, semantically grounded indoor 3D data and the under-constrained nature of sparse panoramas.
Uses correspondence-guided geometric optimization to turn reconstruction priors into cross-view constraints and build coherent 3D Gaussian Splatting spatial memory.
Applies image and video generation priors to restore appearance and complete continuous trajectories while preserving observed content.
Provides RGB-D rendering and automated 3D curation with grounding and VLM-based verification.
Introduces over 1K scenes, 100K+ instance annotations, 2M spatial QA pairs, and a benchmark; fine-tuning on the data improves VLM spatial reasoning.
papers.selection_reason: Generative reconstruction of multi-room 3D environments and benchmark for VLM spatial reasoning, directly relevant to spatial intelligence.
papers.title: Holi-Spatial 360: Generative Reconstruction from Sparse Panoramas for Spatial Rendering and Intelligence
papers.tldr: Holi-Spatial 360 reconstructs richly annotated multi-room 3D environments from sparse real-estate panoramas and uses them to improve spatial reasoning in vision-language models.

papers.abstract: Native multimodal pre-training trains a single model from scratch on text and multimodal data, enabling it to understand both language and visual inputs. However, how visual signals shape scaling behavior and support capabilities beyond visual understanding remains unclear. We investigate this question through controlled visual-content ablations across model sizes and training budgets. Specifically, we replace image embeddings with content-free padding token embeddings. Retaining visual content improves text prediction on image-text examples without materially changing the lowest text-only loss at a given compute budget, the optimal balance of model size and training data, or aggregate language scores. The relative multimodal loss benefit grows approximately as a power law of compute. To test benefits beyond understanding images, we evaluate spatial reasoning from text descriptions alone. Both conditions improve with model and data scaling. During training of the largest model, visual gains are most sustained in localization, navigation, and symbolic planning, which involve maintaining object configurations or composing spatial updates; gains in spatial relations, geometry, and physical commonsense are less consistent. These findings identify visual content as a scalable anchor for multimodal learning, with benefits that extend beyond visual inputs while preserving aggregate language performance.
authors: Haoyuan Wu, Aoqi Wu, Jiani Hu, Bei Yu
bullets: Controlled ablations replace image embeddings with content-free padding embeddings across model sizes and compute budgets.
Retaining visual content improves text prediction on image-text examples, with benefits growing approximately as a power law of compute.
Visual content does not materially change the lowest text-only loss, optimal model/data balance, or aggregate language scores.
Text-only spatial reasoning benefits most consistently in localization, navigation, and symbolic planning, while gains in geometry and physical commonsense are less consistent.
papers.selection_reason: Native multimodal pretraining analysis showing visual content benefits spatial reasoning, fitting multimodal and spatial intelligence interests.
papers.title: More Than Seeing: Vision as Scalable Anchors in Native Multimodal Pre-Training
papers.tldr: Visual content acts as a scalable anchor in native multimodal pre-training, improving multimodal learning and some text-only spatial reasoning without reducing overall language performance.

papers.abstract: Existing illumination estimation methods primarily recover lighting distributions for rendering, but typically leave the contributions of individual physical light sources at specific scene locations implicit. We address this gap by leveraging the scene understanding capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) to connect local illumination with its physical sources. We introduce LAMP, a framework for point-conditioned, source-aware illumination reasoning from a single RGB image with marked query points. LAMP constructs a shared inventory of active light sources, ranks contributing sources for each query, and predicts their 3D query-to-source directions. We supervise these relationships using procedurally controlled indoor scenes, reusing independently rendered source responses to derive contribution targets across lighting configurations and obtaining exact directions from source and query positions. On the Infinigen test set, fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B increases dominant-source 3D PCK@0.5m from 0% to 70.6%, with 94.5% of directions within 12.5 degrees of ground truth among correctly localized sources. Combined with a lightweight network predicting dense RGB irradiance, LAMP achieves probe-rendering quality comparable to prior lighting-estimation methods while additionally localizing individual physical sources in 3D and explicitly attributing local illumination to them.
bullets: Addresses the lack of explicit source attribution in conventional illumination-estimation methods.
Builds a shared inventory of active light sources, ranks their contributions per query point, and predicts 3D query-to-source directions.
Trains on procedurally controlled indoor scenes with source-response contribution targets and exact geometric directions.
On Infinigen, fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-8B reaches 70.6% dominant-source 3D PCK@0.5m; 94.5% of correctly localized directions are within 12.5° of ground truth.
Combined with dense RGB irradiance prediction, achieves probe-rendering quality comparable to prior methods while adding explicit 3D source localization and attribution.
papers.selection_reason: VLM-based 3D source-aware lighting estimation with spatial reasoning, relevant to spatial intelligence.
papers.title: LAMP: 3D Source-Aware Lighting Estimation at Multiple Points
papers.tldr: LAMP uses vision-language models to identify and localize the physical light sources contributing to illumination at multiple 3D query points from a single RGB image.

papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have been widely applied in embodied agents and robotics for vision tasks. However, MLLMs suffer from limitations in spatial reasoning and perception. Post-training techniques have shown promise for improving these capabilities; yet, there are limited data-driven surveys of such approaches. In this survey, we consider approaches to fine-tuning pretrained MLLMs for spatial reasoning tasks, ranging from supervised to reinforcement learning, with an emphasis on the datasets used. We investigate themes of dataset construction, data modality and annotation, and evaluation of the resulting models. Based on these themes, we categorize research into three groups: dataset design, dataset construction and evaluation. We find four main methods for constructing fixed spatial annotations: rules and templates, LLM prompting, procedural generation, and human-in-the-loop. We also observe substantial variation in evaluation approaches, including different scoring methods, tolerance metrics, and benchmark types. Finally, we identify opportunities for future research in unified dynamic annotation, efficient spatial reasoning, standardization of evaluation, expanded spatial range, and human-centered spatial interactions.
authors: Mahdieh Mallahnezhad, Masoud Jafaripour, Mohamadali Tofigh, Sheila Schoepp, Osmar R. Zaiane
bullets: Reviews supervised- and reinforcement-learning approaches for fine-tuning pretrained MLLMs on spatial reasoning tasks.
Categorizes research into dataset design, dataset construction, and evaluation.
Identifies four fixed-annotation strategies: rules and templates, LLM prompting, procedural generation, and human-in-the-loop methods.
Highlights substantial variation in scoring, tolerance metrics, and benchmark types.
Proposes future directions including dynamic annotation, efficient reasoning, standardized evaluation, broader spatial ranges, and human-centered interaction.
papers.selection_reason: Survey of data-centric spatial reasoning fine-tuning for MLLMs.
papers.title: Towards a Data-Centric Understanding of Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.tldr: A data-centric survey organizes how datasets and annotations shape post-training for spatial reasoning in multimodal large language models (MLLMs).

papers.abstract: Aerial and remote sensing video is increasingly evaluated like web video, by posing multiple-choice questions to multimodal large language models (MLLMs) over sampled frames and reporting accuracy. This paper argues that this recipe measures the wrong aspect, and supports the claim with a convergent meta-analysis of a broad set of published results, organized in four evidence tiers, in which a claim becomes a position only when collected evidence agrees. Parameter scale exhibits a median of +3.4 accuracy points per tenfold increase on aerial benchmarks, far below a human gap of at least 19 points, whereas acquisition conditions control perception, as 315 of 318 evaluations in 19 within-paper contrasts lose accuracy when conditions such as altitude, view, object size or time horizon become harder. No aerial benchmark in the corpus combines video input with per-task human and random baselines, competence collapses from answering to acting in closed-loop navigation, and the same MLLMs score higher on the aerial benchmark than on ground spatial ones, but lower on studies that test cross-view geometry. From these findings the current study derives five falsifiable principles and proposes the AVU-Card, a reporting card for aerial video benchmarks
authors: Georgios Angelidis, Aggelos Psiris, Maria Vakalopoulou, Georgios Th. Papadopoulos, Giorgos Sfikas, Iraklis Varlamis
bullets: A convergent meta-analysis synthesizes published aerial and remote-sensing video results across four evidence tiers.
Model parameter scaling yields limited gains: a median +3.4 accuracy points per tenfold increase, versus a human gap of at least 19 points.
Perception degrades in 315 of 318 within-paper contrasts when altitude, viewpoint, object size, or time horizon becomes harder.
Current benchmarks lack video-input evaluations with both task-specific human and random baselines, and competence drops sharply from answering to closed-loop navigation.
The paper proposes five falsifiable principles and the AVU-Card for reporting aerial video benchmark properties.
papers.selection_reason: Meta-analysis of MLLM aerial video understanding and geometry, relevant to spatial and video evaluation.
papers.title: The Gap Is in the Geometry: A Convergent Meta-Analysis of Multi-Facet Aerial and Remote Sensing Video Understanding
papers.tldr: Aerial video benchmarks often measure acquisition-condition sensitivity rather than genuine spatial understanding, motivating geometry-focused evaluation and standardized reporting.

papers.abstract: Constructing robust GUI agents relies on multimodal visual grounding: the ability to precisely map natural language intents to actionable on-screen components. Despite abundant desktop, web, and mobile benchmarks, high-fidelity resources tailored for diverse environments are surprisingly scarce. To bridge this gap, we introduce the Screen Referring Grounding Dataset (ScreenRef), a comprehensive GUI grounding dataset consisting of GUI screenshots paired with natural language referring expressions and box or point annotations. Spanning desktop, web, and mobile domains, ScreenRef comprises 586K screenshots and over 633K referring expression instances, covering tasks such as text recognition, visual matching, spatial understanding, and refusal scenarios. To boost the model's grounding performance, we propose the Distillation-to-Reinforcement Learning (D2RL) method to address the limited generalization of supervised fine-tuning and the sparse reward problem in reinforcement learning. Utilizing ScreenRef, we train Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct via sequential SFT and D2RL training, yielding GroundGUI-8B. GroundGUI-8B achieves 95.2% on ScreenSpot-V2, 63.9% on ScreenSpot-Pro, 65.4% on OSWorld-G, 86.8% on MMBench-GUI L2, and 38.3% on UI-Vision. Among 8B-scale models, it produces substantial gains over models trained on open-source datasets, with performance comparable or even superior to models trained on closed-source data. Code, models, and datasets are available at https://github.com/PrentisAI/GroundGUI.
authors: Qingsong Xie, Jiahao Tian, Jiacheng Tang, Zhifeng Li, Madalina Ciobanu, Navan Preet Singh, Qingqing Mao, Ritankar Das
bullets: ScreenRef contains 586K GUI screenshots and over 633K referring-expression instances across desktop, web, and mobile environments.
The dataset supports text recognition, visual matching, spatial understanding, and refusal scenarios using box or point annotations.
The proposed D2RL method targets limited generalization from supervised fine-tuning and sparse rewards in reinforcement learning.
GroundGUI-8B, trained from Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, reports strong results across five GUI grounding benchmarks.
The work provides the ScreenRef dataset, trained models, and code publicly.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces GroundGUI, a method for GUI grounding using a large dataset (ScreenRef) and Distillation-to-Reinforcement Learning. This advances multimodal VLMs (Qwen3-VL) in spatial understanding and grounding tasks.
papers.title: GroundGUI: GUI Grounding by High-Quality Data and Distillation-to-Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: GroundGUI improves GUI grounding by combining a large, diverse annotated dataset with sequential supervised and distillation-to-reinforcement learning.

papers.abstract: Modern image generation largely relies on specialized generative models that leave the process of image construction implicit in learned parameters. We explore an alternative: general-purpose coding agents that construct images through executable programs. Our study of zero-shot drawing on AgentDrawBench, a 200-prompt benchmark, reveals a distinctive capability profile. Agents excel at preserving structure and satisfying precise visual constraints, achieving competitive results in domains where compositional accuracy matters more than photorealistic appearance, while remaining limited in perceptual richness. Their visual expressiveness varies with the drawing interface, and a qualitative study on reconstruction shows how procedural skills extracted from human demonstrations support different artistic media. We then examine code as an external visual language of thought: a structured, executable representation that agents can construct and inspect. We test it in visual question answering task and find reconstructed visual code retains substantial information for question answering and, in some domains, supports higher accuracy than the original image. These abilities raise a further question: do agents draw on a shared internal representation of scene content beyond a particular drawing program? We explore an internal visual language-of-thought hypothesis, in which a shared, compositionally structured representation supports visual operations across drawing languages. Cross-harness drawings and images assembled from independent single-pixel queries exhibit related layouts and tones. Agents also maintain self-generated room arrangements across viewpoints after visible drawings are removed. These results demonstrate that the coding agent would maintain a consistent and coherent world inside its imagine even before the harness gets involved and the generation starts.
authors: Hengguang Zhou, Yuanhao Ban, Jiaqi Feng, Xiaohuan Pei, Justin Cui, Cho-Jui Hsieh
bullets: On the 200-prompt AgentDrawBench, agents perform well when compositional accuracy and precise constraints matter more than photorealism.
Their expressiveness depends on the drawing interface, while procedural skills from human demonstrations transfer across artistic media.
Executable visual code retains substantial information for visual question answering and can outperform the original image in some domains.
Cross-harness and single-pixel experiments suggest agents maintain a shared, compositionally structured internal representation of scenes.
The findings indicate coherent scene understanding before image generation begins, though perceptual richness remains a limitation.
papers.selection_reason: Explores code as visual language of thought and internal scene consistency, transferable to multimodal and spatial reasoning.
papers.title: How Far Can Coding Agents Go in Visual Generation?
papers.tldr: Coding agents can generate structurally precise, executable visual representations and preserve scene information, but their visual richness remains limited.

papers.abstract: 3D part assembly aims to reconstruct a complete shape from a set of unassembled parts by predicting a rigid SE(3) transformation for each part. Because the placement of a part is rarely determined by its own geometry, the task demands reasoning over the entire part set, and existing methods, which rely on pairwise relations or iterative generation and verification, scale poorly to objects with many parts. We present LLM2R, which casts part assembly as sequence modeling with a pretrained decoder-only large language model (LLM): a Point-BERT encoder and a Q-Former compress each part into a block of geometric tokens, the blocks of all parts are concatenated, and a causal LLM adapted with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) processes the sequence in one forward pass. Causal attention, however, lets the hidden states of a part observe only the parts that precede it. LLM2R therefore appends a block of learnable summary tokens after the last part: these tokens follow every part, so their states aggregate the whole assembly at a constant token cost, and a part-aware pose head fuses each part's states with them before predicting its rotation and translation. One architecture thus handles semantic and geometric assembly and predicts all poses in a single non-autoregressive pass. LLM2R achieves the highest part accuracy and success rate on all three PartNet categories, the best rotation error, translation error, and part accuracy on PartNeXt, and the lowest translation error and fastest inference on Breaking Bad, where only a fracture-specialized method is more accurate. Its advantage grows with the number of parts: at 100 parts it exceeds GARF by 33.5 points in part accuracy on Breaking Bad and Assembler by 29.1 points on PartNet, and it transfers zero-shot to unseen categories with more than 16 points higher part accuracy than the strongest of three baselines.
authors: Zhouhan Zhong, Qiuhong Shen, Xingyi Yang, Jinyi Xu, Xinchao Wang
bullets: Problem: Pairwise and iterative assembly methods struggle as the number of parts grows because placement depends on the full set.
Method: Point-BERT and a Q-Former encode each part into geometric-token blocks, which a LoRA-adapted causal LLM processes in one pass.
Key design: Learnable summary tokens aggregate information from all parts and are fused with each part’s states to predict rotation and translation.
Results: LLM2R achieves leading or competitive accuracy, pose errors, success rate, and inference speed across PartNet, PartNeXt, and Breaking Bad.
Scope: It transfers zero-shot to unseen categories and its advantage increases for assemblies with many parts.
papers.selection_reason: LLM-based 3D part assembly with geometric token sequence modeling; relevant to 3D foundation models and spatial reasoning.
papers.title: LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers
papers.tldr: LLM2R reframes 3D part assembly as one-pass sequence modeling with an LLM, enabling scalable prediction of all part poses using global assembly context.

papers.abstract: Geospatial reasoning links VLMs to real-world action and decision making. Reliable reasoning requires accurate spatial information and effective spatial representations. However, current VLMs obtain this information mainly from language and vision. At larger geographic scales, limited visual observations make it difficult to establish accurate spatial references and recover precise spatial relations. This leads to a bottleneck for VLM spatial perception and reasoning. This paper proposes that geospatial vector geometry can become a native spatial modality within a VLM and introduces GeoVec-VLM. First, we develop a structured geometry representation that preserves the spatial structure and arrangement of vector objects, building an explicit spatial basis. Second, we introduce a geometry interaction strategy that brings this basis into multimodal computation, where it interacts with visual content and language references according to the queried spatial relations. Together, these designs allow perception and reasoning to operate on shared geometric references. Across five spatial reasoning tasks, GeoVec-VLM improves mean accuracy by about 11\% relative to the strongest baseline, maintains its gains under geographic transfer, and shows greater geometric consistency. Our results show that geospatial vector geometry offers a promising internal spatial basis for VLM spatial reasoning. https://github.com/TXFR/GeoVector-VLM
authors: Huang Fei, Boyi Chen, Hao Xue, Yang Yue, Yehong Xu, Xiaofang Zhou
bullets: Current VLMs struggle with precise spatial references at large geographic scales because visual observations are limited.
The model uses a structured geometry representation that preserves vector-object arrangements as an explicit spatial basis.
A geometry interaction strategy combines this basis with visual content and language references based on queried spatial relations.
Across five spatial reasoning tasks, it improves mean accuracy by about 11% over the strongest baseline and retains gains under geographic transfer.
The model also demonstrates greater geometric consistency, supporting vector geometry as an internal basis for VLM reasoning.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces geospatial vector geometry as a native spatial modality for VLMs, directly advancing spatial reasoning in multimodal models.
papers.title: Geospatial Vector Geometry as a Native Spatial Modality for Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: GeoVec-VLM integrates geospatial vector geometry as a native spatial modality to improve large-scale spatial perception and reasoning in vision-language models.

papers.abstract: We present Co-DSL, a framework in which users and LLMs co-design reusable spatial concepts for layout generation. In the first stage, our system allows users to create a library of personalized operations. To add a concept, a user provides a description, which the LLM converts into an initial implementation. The user can then observe the concept's execution behavior over example scenarios and provide lightweight feedback to the LLM, which revises the concept's implementation logic. In the second stage, given a library, an LLM can author a layout program that meets a new layout request from a user. Executing a layout program instantiates a concept-graph, a declarative composition of library concepts. In this way, we require the LLM only to specify which concepts should hold, while we use a solver to search for a layout that satisfies them. Across five spatial layout domains, we find that Co-DSL libraries let LLMs capture layout patterns that are challenging for prior fixed-operation systems, and demonstrate that our concept-graph representation is needed for LLMs to reliably compose concepts together. We further find that Co-DSL lets LLMs author generative layout programs that expose high-level parametric controls users can manipulate to explore a distribution of related layouts without re-prompting.
authors: R. Kenny Jones, Jiajun Wu, Maneesh Agrawala
bullets: Users describe personalized spatial operations; the LLM implements and revises them based on lightweight feedback and observed examples.
For new requests, the LLM authors a layout program represented as a concept graph, specifying which concepts should hold.
A solver searches for layouts satisfying the composed concepts, reducing the need for the LLM to generate exact layouts directly.
Across five spatial layout domains, the framework captures patterns beyond fixed-operation systems and reliably composes concepts.
Generated programs expose parametric controls for exploring related layouts without repeated prompting.
papers.selection_reason: Human-LLM co-design of reusable spatial concepts for layout generation, relevant to spatial intelligence.
papers.title: Co-DSL: Human-LLM Co-design of Reusable Spatial Concepts for Layout Generation
papers.tldr: Co-DSL lets users and LLMs collaboratively create reusable spatial concepts that LLMs compose into solver-generated layouts with high-level controls.

papers.abstract: A GUI agent decides which action to take and where to take it; we ask how a small grounding model should receive the action type. Fine-tuning Qwen2-VL-2B with LoRA on Android in the Wild, we compare a flat baseline with five ways of supplying the type under matched data, compute, and decoding: an auxiliary loss, a hard-routed action word, an additive learned embedding, a prepended learned token, and the type written into the prompt. With five seeds, an episode-clustered bootstrap, and seed-level paired tests, the ranking on a mixed stream is clear: the auxiliary loss, the additive embedding, and the prompt word each gain five to seven hit@0.10 points over the baseline, while hard routing and the prepended token are not distinguishable from it. Much of that gain is protection from a preprocessing choice of ours rather than a spatial prior. Our serializer clamps the off-screen touch point AITW records for type events to the origin; that class degrades the baseline's click grounding, and removing it lifts the baseline by nearly seven points, after which no mechanism's hit rate beats it and the intervals exclude a two-point effect, though the auxiliary loss still shortens the average miss; on a stream of taps and swipes none helps. Whether this generalizes beyond one serialization is open. For deployment, the pipeline's margin over the baseline with predicted rather than gold types is not established (+0.016, 95% interval [-0.017, +0.052]), and a wrong type collapses every model conditioned at inference. The prepended token does not help at the shared learning rate, where its rows barely move from initialization; trained ten times faster it reaches the level of the other three, with a margin three seeds do not establish. We also document a silent failure: injecting conditioning through inputs_embeds makes Qwen2-VL fall back to 1-D positions for image tokens, costing nine points.
bullets: Fine-tuning Qwen2-VL-2B with LoRA compared five conditioning mechanisms against a flat baseline under matched settings.
Auxiliary loss, additive embedding, and prompt-word conditioning initially improved mixed-stream hit@0.10 by 5–7 points; hard routing and a prepended token did not.

Clamping off-screen touch points to the origin caused much of the apparent gain: after removing this artifact, no method outperformed the baseline, though auxiliary loss reduced average miss distance.
No method helped on taps and swipes; predicted action types gave no established deployment margin, and wrong types degraded all conditioned models.
A separate inputs_embeds implementation issue caused 1-D image-token positions and a nine-point performance loss; generalization beyond this serialization remains open.
papers.selection_reason: Investigates how to condition GUI grounding models on action types, relevant to spatial intelligence and multimodal models.
papers.title: Decoupling What from Where: How Should a Small GUI Grounding Model Receive the Action Type?
papers.tldr: For a small GUI grounding model, action-type conditioning appears helpful mainly because of a preprocessing artifact, not a robust spatial benefit.

papers.abstract: Generative vision-language models (VLMs) such as Qwen-VL and LLaVA achieve strong zero-shot performance on tasks overlapping with their pretraining distribution, yet fail on specialized domains where the required discriminative features were never learned, a regime we term distant out-of-distribution (OOD). Standard adaptation methods cannot overcome this representational absence because they operate within the encoder's existing feature space. However, VLMs retain a robust descriptive capacity even when discrimination collapses: a model that cannot classify a medical scan can still articulate its visual patterns. Exploiting this asymmetry, we introduce Inductive Visual Logic (IVL), a training-free framework that constructs classification knowledge from the model's surviving descriptive ability. IVL extracts visual traits from few-shot support images through dual-mode prompting, combining semantic descriptions with primitive visual observations, and organizes them into per-class trait dictionaries. At inference, hierarchical filtering identifies spatially grounded trait evidence for classification. Across multiple distant-OOD benchmarks, IVL achieves the highest aggregate accuracy under two VLM backbones while producing interpretable, trait-traceable predictions.
bullets: Addresses distant OOD settings where required discriminative features are absent from the VLM’s learned representation.
Uses dual-mode prompting to extract semantic and primitive visual traits from few-shot support images.
Builds per-class trait dictionaries and applies hierarchical, spatially grounded trait filtering at inference.
Achieves the highest aggregate accuracy across multiple distant-OOD benchmarks with two VLM backbones.
Produces interpretable predictions that can be traced to visual traits.
